stem: A pipeline declares a streaming table with one expectation named valid_customer_age. A downstream report still shows ages above 120, so invalid records are clearly reaching the target. The pipeline must keep running while invalid records stop reaching the target, and the team needs to know why the current declaration retains them.

option_texts.A: Rewrite the clause as EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE so an invalid record stops the update
option_texts.B: Rewrite the query to filter the rows in SQL, because expectations cannot remove records from the target
option_texts.C: Rewrite the clause as EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW, because a bare EXPECT writes invalid records to the target
option_texts.D: Rewrite the expectation with a second constraint name, because one name per dataset only warns

drill_answer_short: warn is the default action, so a bare EXPECT still writes invalid records to the target; ON VIOLATION DROP ROW drops them
decision_hinge: warn is the default action and invalid records are written to the target; EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW means invalid records are dropped before data is written to the target.

plausible_options.A: invalid records stop reaching the target

eliminated_by.B: the team needs to know why the current declaration retains them
eliminated_by.D: A downstream report still shows ages above 120

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - FAIL UPDATE stops the update instead of letting the pipeline keep running
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - expectations can drop invalid records, so a hand-written SQL filter is not the fix
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the expectation name is an identifier and never controls the action on invalid records

stem: A silver transformation calls explode on a tags column so each array element becomes its own row. Some source records carry a NULL tags value, and the audit shows those records vanish from the silver table entirely. The transformation must preserve one row per source record even when the collection is NULL.

option_texts.A: Call explode_outer, which returns a single row with NULLs when the collection is NULL
option_texts.B: Call posexplode, which returns the element position next to each exploded value
option_texts.C: Call inline, which expands a collection of structs into separate output columns
option_texts.D: Call flatten first, which merges the nested arrays before the generator runs

drill_answer_short: explode produces no rows for a NULL collection; explode_outer returns a single row with NULLs instead
decision_hinge: If collection is NULL no rows are produced by explode; to return a single row with NULLs for the array or map values use the explode_outer function.

plausible_options.B: each array element becomes its own row

eliminated_by.C: Some source records carry a NULL tags value
eliminated_by.D: the audit shows those records vanish from the silver table entirely

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - posexplode adds the position but still produces no rows for a NULL collection
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - inline is another generator function and drops a NULL collection just as explode does
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - flatten merges nested arrays and never restores a row for a NULL collection

stem: A pipeline joins a streaming bookings source to a slowly-changing users table stored in Delta Lake. The design must avoid any state the engine has to track between micro-batches, and the team is deciding whether this join requires watermarks on both sides.

option_texts.A: Configure watermarks on both sides, because any join that reads a stream is stateful
option_texts.B: Configure a watermark on the streaming side only, because a static side cannot carry one
option_texts.C: Configure the users table as a second stream, so both sides of the join match in type
option_texts.D: Configure no watermarks, because a stream-static join is stateless and reads the latest version of the static table

drill_answer_short: A stream-static join is stateless, so no watermarking is needed; each micro-batch joins the latest valid version of the static Delta table
decision_hinge: Stream-static joins are stateless, so you don't need to configure watermarking, and the latest valid version of data from the static Delta table joins with the records present in the current micro-batch.

plausible_options.A: whether this join requires watermarks on both sides

eliminated_by.B: a slowly-changing users table stored in Delta Lake
eliminated_by.C: The design must avoid any state the engine has to track between micro-batches

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - stream-stream joins are stateful and do want watermarks on both sides, a stream-static join does not
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - there is no partial watermark rule that applies to the streaming side of a stateless join
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - promoting the static side to a stream makes the join stateful

stem: A nightly job runs a large sort merge join on a current Databricks runtime with default settings. One task runs far longer than the rest because a few join keys dominate the data. An engineer proposes adding a skew join hint, and the team must decide whether that hint is required.

option_texts.A: Add the skew hint, because skew handling stays off until a hint names the skewed column
option_texts.B: Add nothing, because AQE already splits the skewed tasks into roughly evenly sized tasks
option_texts.C: Add a repartition on the join key, because splitting can only happen before the shuffle
option_texts.D: Add a broadcast hint, because broadcasting the larger side of the join removes the skew

drill_answer_short: AQE handles skew in sort merge join automatically, so a skew join hint is not required
decision_hinge: AQE dynamically handles skew in sort merge join and shuffle hash join by splitting and replicating skewed tasks into roughly evenly sized tasks.

plausible_options.A: An engineer proposes adding a skew join hint

eliminated_by.C: One task runs far longer than the rest because a few join keys dominate the data
eliminated_by.D: a current Databricks runtime with default settings

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - hints exist for range joins, but skew handling is automatic and needs no hint
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - AQE re-optimizes using runtime statistics after the shuffle exchange, not only before it
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - broadcasting the larger side of a join is not a skew remedy

stem: A gold materialized view was defined once with a long CREATE OR REPLACE statement. An on-call engineer must bring it up to date after an unscheduled backfill of the base table, and must do so without pasting the defining query again.

option_texts.A: Run CREATE OR REPLACE MATERIALIZED VIEW again, supplying the full defining query
option_texts.B: Run OPTIMIZE on the materialized view so that it picks up the new base table files
option_texts.C: Run REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, which updates the view to reflect the latest changes to the base table
option_texts.D: Run DROP and recreate, because a materialized view cannot be brought up to date on demand

drill_answer_short: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW updates the view to the latest base-table changes without resupplying the query
decision_hinge: Refreshing a materialized view updates the view to reflect the latest changes to the base table at the time of the refresh, and you can use the REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW statement without needing to supply the query again.

plausible_options.A: must bring it up to date after an unscheduled backfill of the base table

eliminated_by.B: A gold materialized view was defined once with a long CREATE OR REPLACE statement
eliminated_by.D: must do so without pasting the defining query again

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the same statement does serve scheduled refreshes, but it means supplying the query again
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - OPTIMIZE rewrites file layout and never recomputes the view against the base table
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a materialized view supports an on-demand refresh, so dropping it is unnecessary
